construction_rule: Provider-independent. Anchors admitted only after independent verification against publisher article page, PubMed/PMC, FlyBase, Virtual Fly Brain, Monarch Initiative, or the Janelia dataset documentation. Crossref metadata used only to confirm identity after primary verification is complete (per Reopen Prompt §2).

anchors.canonical_title: A spike-timing mechanism for action selection
anchors.relation_to_question: Q1 + Q2 + Q3. Original Giant Fiber physiology / action-selection source lineage. First intracellular recording of the descending Giant Fiber interneuron during head-fixed escape; defines GF as the descending interneuron that controls the long-duration escape behavior. Published June 2014 (online) / July 2014 (print).
oracle_source: FlyBase reference report: https://flybase.org/reports/FBrf0225495 (FlyBase ID FBrf0225495)
anchors.oracle_verification_note: Metadata (title, authors, journal, year, volume/issue/pages, DOI, PMID) independently confirmed against PubMed, Europe PMC, Janelia bibliography, and FlyBase reference report FBrf0225495. Four independent primary sources agree. The 2014 publication date is the citation-of-record for the 'von Reyn 2014' reference; the von Reyn name in the GF/EM task refers to first author Catherine R. von Reyn.

anchors.canonical_title: The functional organization of descending sensory-motor pathways in Drosophila
anchors.relation_to_question: Q2 + Q4. Standardized descending-neuron nomenclature. The paper labels the Giant Fiber as 'DNp01' (descending neuron of the posterior brain, type 01) within the broader DN cell-type catalog. It is the authoritative source for the GF / Giant Fiber / DNp01 naming lineage. Note: the 'DNg01' label that may appear in some pre-2018 literature is NOT a synonym of DNp01 according to the 3 scholarly oracle anchors; the oracle's active stance on DNg01 is UNRESOLVED / DISTINCT_NEURON_CLASS_UNLESS_AUTHORITATIVE_EVIDENCE (see nomenclature_uncertainties.DNg01 below).
oracle_source: Commentary (also eLife 2018): https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.38410 (Descending neurons: Disentangling the strings that organize behavior)
anchors.oracle_verification_note: Metadata independently confirmed against PubMed (PMID 29943730), PMC (PMCID PMC6019073), and eLife DOI 10.7554/eLife.34272. Three independent primary sources agree. The DNp01 nomenclature mapping is also confirmed in the Virtual Fly Brain entry for FBbt:00004020 and the Monarch Initiative giant fiber neuron record.

anchors.canonical_title: A connectome and analysis of the adult Drosophila central brain
authors: et al. (full author list in publication)
anchors.relation_to_question: Q4. The hemibrain connectome publication. Establishes the dense reconstruction of the central portion of the adult Drosophila brain (~25,000 neurons, ~20 million chemical synapses). The hemibrain dataset v1.1 / v1.2.1 is the empirical basis for any hemibrain-rooted GF body ID.
anchors.oracle_verification_note: Metadata independently confirmed against PubMed (PMID 32880371), eLife DOI 10.7554/eLife.57443, and the Janelia publication record. Three independent primary sources agree. Publication date 2020-09-07.

DNg01.claim_in_question: DNg01 is a synonym / older label for the same neuron as GF / Giant Fiber / DNp01
DNg01.rule: Per Reopen-RA1 contract §2, unless authoritative primary-source evidence establishes that DNg01 is a synonym for DNp01, DNg01 is treated as a DISTINCT neuron class. No primary source among the 3 scholarly oracle anchors (PubMed/Europe PMC/FlyBase FBrf0225495, PubMed/PMC/eLife DOI, PubMed/eLife DOI) establishes this synonymy. VFB FBbt:00004020 and Monarch Initiative both reference 'DNp01' as the modern identifier; neither asserts that 'DNg01' is the same neuron.
DNg01.reopens: Replay B Reopen-RA1 §2 (this section), Reopen Prompt §1, original Replay B contract §2 Q2 text.

negative_branch.description: The user request includes 'von Reyn et al. 2014/2020 等论文' — i.e., a 2020 paper by von Reyn is implied. Per Reopen Prompt §7, this is a first-class negative/correction benchmark. Crossref / PubMed / Google Scholar searches for 'von Reyn CR' + '2020' + 'Drosophila' do not return a 2020 von Reyn GF/EM publication; the canonical 2014 paper remains the citation-of-record.
negative_branch.note: The 'von Reyn 2020 GF paper' is a conflation with the later hemibrain / connectome work (Scheffer 2020) or with broader Drosophila neuroscience from 2020 onwards, but no von Reyn 2020 GF/EM primary publication exists. This is reported as a NOT_FOUND result, not a fabrication.
